field_of_use: lab proposer-responder game with reward/punish options
title: The Carrot or the Stick: Rewards, Punishments, and Cooperation
description: Responder may reward, punish, or both after proposer's offer.
evidence: Punishment alone and reward alone each modestly raise offers; combination most effective; rewards and punishment are complements.

title: Communication and Cooperation in Social Dilemmas: A Meta-Analytic Review
description: Pre-play communication (cheap talk) among dilemma participants, face-to-face versus written.
evidence: Large positive effect of communication on cooperation; face-to-face much stronger than written; larger groups weaken effect.

title: Vaccination and the theory of games
description: Game-theoretic analysis showing voluntary vaccination is a public good subject to free-riding.
evidence: Theory: voluntary coverage below eradication level.

title: Rotating Savings and Credit Associations, Credit Markets and Efficiency
description: Random and bidding ROSCAs allocate the pot; social sanctions deter default by early recipients.
evidence: Theoretical welfare comparison with credit markets.

title: Egalitarian Behavior and Reverse Dominance Hierarchy
description: Reverse dominance hierarchy: the group collectively uses ridicule, criticism, ostracism, and execution to curb would-be dominants.
evidence: Cross-cultural survey (descriptive).

title: Promoting Compliance with Human Rights: The Performance of the United Nations' Universal Periodic Review and Treaty Bodies
description: Peer review of states by states (UPR) and expert treaty-body review generate pressure and learning.
evidence: Interviews: UPR perceived as generating stronger pressure (political, peer-based) while treaty bodies stronger on expertise.

title: Punishment in animal societies
description: Retaliatory aggression that reduces the payoffs of cheating, parasitism, or failure to cooperate.
evidence: Review and models.

title: Can Catch Shares Prevent Fisheries Collapse?
description: Catch shares (ITQs): rights-based individual quotas of total allowable catch.
evidence: Catch shares halt, and even reverse, the global trend toward collapse.

title: Is the good news about compliance good news about cooperation?
description: Enforcement school: high compliance reflects shallow agreements; deeper cooperation requires credible punishment.
evidence: Argument: selection effects make compliance rates uninformative about enforcement need.

title: Signaling Foreign Policy Interests: Tying Hands versus Sinking Costs
description: Hand-tying (public commitments generating audience costs) versus sinking costs (costly mobilization) as credible signals.
evidence: Theoretical.

field_of_use: lab dictator and PD games with an unaffected third party
title: Third-party punishment and social norms
description: Unaffected third parties can pay to punish norm violators (unfair dictators, defectors).
evidence: Many third parties punish violations of distribution and cooperation norms, though less than second parties.

title: Local Enforcement and Better Forests
description: Regular local monitoring and sanctioning of forest rules by user groups.
evidence: Rule enforcement strongly associated with better forest conditions.

field_of_use: lab public-goods game with choice between sanctioning and sanction-free institution
title: The Competitive Advantage of Sanctioning Institutions
description: Participants repeatedly choose whether to play in a community with peer sanctioning/reward or one without; migration between institutions.
evidence: Initially most avoid sanctions, but the sanctioning institution eventually attracts nearly everyone and sustains full cooperation.

title: Managing Drug Involved Probationers with Swift and Certain Sanctions: Evaluating Hawaii's HOPE
description: Swift, certain, modest sanctions (brief jail) for each probation violation.
evidence: RCT: fewer positive drug tests, missed appointments, and revocations.

title: Cash for carbon: A randomized trial of payments for ecosystem services to reduce deforestation
description: Payments for ecosystem services conditional on not clearing trees.
evidence: Tree cover loss reduced; no leakage to neighbors; benefits exceed costs.

field_of_use: COVID-19 vaccine passports, Canada and Europe
title: COVID-19 vaccination mandates and vaccine uptake
description: Vaccination mandates/passports conditioning access to venues on proof of vaccination.
evidence: Mandate announcements associated with sharp increases in first-dose uptake.

title: The Rational Design of International Institutions
description: Institutional design choices (membership, scope, centralization, control, flexibility) chosen to solve enforcement and uncertainty problems.
evidence: Conjectures, tested in special issue.

title: Performance Pay and Productivity
description: Switch from hourly wages to piece-rate pay.
evidence: Productivity up ~44% (half incentive, half sorting).

title: The Role of Institutions in the Revival of Trade: The Law Merchant, Private Judges, and the Champagne Fairs
description: Law merchant: private judges record disputes and past judgments, and traders query them before trading, enabling community enforcement among strangers.
evidence: Model shows the institution sustains honest trade at low information cost.

field_of_use: lab public-goods game with a second retaliation stage
title: Punishment and counter-punishment in public good games: Can we really govern ourselves?
description: Adds a counter-punishment stage in which punished players can retaliate against their punishers.
evidence: Fear of retaliation reduces punishment and cooperation falls relative to punishment-only treatments.

title: Nonmedical Exemptions to School Immunization Requirements: Secular Trends and Association of State Policies With Pertussis Incidence
description: School immunization requirements with religious/personal-belief exemptions.
evidence: States permitting personal-belief exemptions and easy exemption procedures had higher exemption rates and pertussis incidence.

field_of_use: US municipal solid waste and container recycling
title: The Cost of Reducing Municipal Solid Waste
description: Deposit-refund: a deposit paid on purchase refunded upon return of the product for recycling, combining a tax on disposal with a subsidy for recovery.
evidence: Simulation: deposit-refund achieves waste reduction at roughly half the cost of advance disposal fees or recycling subsidies alone.

title: Conflict resolution in insect societies
description: Review of conflict resolution: policing, coercion, and kin structure regulating reproduction and caste.
evidence: Review.

title: The Evolution of Cooperation
description: Three models: directed reciprocation (partner fidelity feedback, partner choice), shared genes, and byproduct benefits.
evidence: Review.

title: The private provision of public goods via dominant assurance contracts
description: Dominant assurance contract: entrepreneur refunds contributions plus a bonus if threshold not met, making contribution dominant.
evidence: Theoretical: contributing becomes a dominant strategy.

title: Reciprocal food sharing in the vampire bat
description: Blood-meal regurgitation to roost-mates, preferentially to kin and to those who previously donated.
evidence: Sharing depends on relatedness and association, consistent with reciprocal altruism.

title: Steering user behavior with badges
description: Formal model and Stack Overflow data on badges as incentives that steer users toward targeted actions.
evidence: Users increase targeted activity as they approach badge thresholds (from memory)

title: STFU NOOB! Predicting crowdsourced decisions on toxic behavior in online games
description: The Tribunal is a two-stage crowdsourced system: players report toxic players, and peer reviewers vote on aggregated reports to decide punishment; paper trains classifiers to predict these decisions.
evidence: 10M+ reports on 1.46M cases; crowd decisions predictable by ML

title: Performance analysis of the CONFIDANT protocol
description: CONFIDANT makes misbehaviour unattractive by detecting and isolating misbehaving nodes; trust and routing decisions use experienced, observed and reported (second-hand) forwarding behaviour, i.e. reputation plus exclusion.
evidence: Simulation: DSR with CONFIDANT outperforms defenseless DSR under misbehaving nodes

title: You Can't Stay Here: The Efficacy of Reddit's 2015 Ban Examined Through Hate Speech
description: Reddit banned r/fatpeoplehate and r/CoonTown for harassment-policy violations: collective removal of a community.
evidence: More accounts than expected left; those staying cut hate speech by at least 80%; receiving subreddits saw no increase

title: Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct v2.1
description: Enforcement guidelines ladder: 1 Correction (private warning), 2 Warning, 3 Temporary Ban, 4 Permanent Ban, applied by community leaders according to impact.
evidence: descriptive

title: The Sybil Attack
description: Shows that without a logically centralised identity-certifying authority, a single faulty entity can present multiple identities, defeating redundancy- and reputation-based mechanisms.
evidence: Theoretical impossibility result

title: Proof-of-stake rewards and penalties
description: Slashable behaviours (double proposals, conflicting attestations) burn up to 1 ETH and force exit over 36 days, with a correlation penalty on day 18 scaled by how many validators were slashed around the same time; attestation rewards pay honest validators.
evidence: descriptive

title: Scaling Consensus: Increasing Decentralization in Wikipedia Governance
description: Interview study showing Wikipedia governance decentralising: rule-making and enforcement increasingly occur in local WikiProjects, echoing Ostrom's design principles for self-governing institutions.
evidence: Qualitative (not re-checked)

title: Limiting interactions in your repository
description: Maintainers can temporarily restrict activity (e.g. to prior contributors or collaborators, or blocking accounts under 24 hours old) for 24 hours to 6 months to cool down heated discussions.
evidence: descriptive

title: Leases: an efficient fault-tolerant mechanism for distributed file cache consistency
description: A lease grants a holder rights (e.g., to cache data) for a bounded time; rights expire automatically unless renewed, so a failed or partitioned holder cannot block others indefinitely.
evidence: Analytic/trace: short leases give consistency with small overhead

title: An integrated trust and reputation model for open multi-agent systems
description: FIRE integrates interaction trust, role-based trust, witness reputation and certified reputation (agent-presented references) to estimate trustworthiness of partners.
evidence: Simulation: agents using FIRE select better partners than benchmarks (not re-checked)

title: A survey of trust and reputation systems for online service provision
description: Survey of trust and reputation computation (summation, Bayesian, discrete, belief, fuzzy, flow models) and centralized vs distributed architectures.
evidence: Survey

title: The EigenTrust algorithm for reputation management in P2P networks
description: Each peer receives a global trust value computed as the left principal eigenvector of normalised local trust ratings (based on past satisfactory downloads), with pre-trusted peers; peers then prefer downloading from high-trust peers.
evidence: Simulations: reduces inauthentic downloads under various collusion threat models

title: Certificate transparency
description: Explains CT as public, verifiable logs of all issued certificates so domain owners and third parties can spot rogue certificates, with browsers requiring proof of logging.
evidence: descriptive

title: Restricting accounts
description: Strike ladder: first strike a warning, 2-6 strikes feature limits, 7 strikes a 1-day content-creation restriction, 8 three days, 9 seven days, 10+ 30 days; continued violation leads to account disabling; severe policies get extra restrictions.
evidence: descriptive

title: Augur: a decentralized oracle and prediction market platform
description: REP token holders report event outcomes; reports agreeing with consensus are rewarded and dissenting reporters lose reputation, turning truthful reporting into a Schelling point.
evidence: descriptive (design)

title: Trust in multi-agent systems
description: Survey distinguishing individual-level trust (learning, reputation, socio-cognitive) from system-level trust mechanisms (protocols making lying irrational, reputation mechanisms, security).
evidence: Survey

title: Internet X.509 PKI Certificate and CRL Profile (RFC 5280)
description: Defines certificate revocation lists by which a CA publishes serial numbers of certificates revoked before expiry (e.g. key compromise), which relying parties check before trusting.
evidence: descriptive (standard)

title: Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) (RFC 7489)
description: Domain owners publish policies (none, quarantine, reject) telling receivers how to treat mail failing SPF/DKIM alignment, plus aggregate reporting back to the domain owner.
evidence: descriptive

title: The protection of information in computer systems
description: Sets out design principles including least privilege, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation and separation of privilege (e.g. requiring two keys), limiting what any program or user can do and the damage from errors or abuse.
evidence: descriptive (design principles)

title: BFT Protocol Forensics
description: Formalises 'forensic support': when faults exceed the tolerance threshold and safety is violated, honest replicas can identify, with cryptographic integrity, as many culpable replicas as possible, enabling ex post accountability.
evidence: Forensic support depends heavily on minor implementation details

title: Code of conduct in open source projects
description: Empirical study of codes of conduct adopted by open-source projects, their content (e.g. derived from Contributor Covenant) and enforcement provisions.
evidence: Descriptive empirical study (not re-checked)

title: Wikipedia:Blocking policy
description: Administrators block accounts to protect the project; blocks are preventive not punitive and 'may escalate in duration if problems recur', and can be appealed.
evidence: descriptive

title: A first look at online reputation on Airbnb, where every stay is above average
description: Compares Airbnb and TripAdvisor ratings of the same properties to assess the informativeness of platform ratings.
evidence: Airbnb ratings are highly concentrated at the top of the scale (from title/memory)

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
description: Lead agent delegates with explicit objectives, output formats, tool guidance and task boundaries, and effort-scaling rules for how many subagents to spawn; outputs graded by LLM-as-judge rubric.
evidence: descriptive; vague delegation caused duplicated work and 50-subagent over-spawning before rules were added

field_of_use: LLM agents outsourcing subtasks to third-party agents
title: COALESCE: Economic and Security Dynamics of Skill-Based Task Outsourcing Among Team of Autonomous LLM Agents
description: Labour exchange with skill-based competence estimation, market-based outsourcing decisions and a standardized inter-agent protocol.
evidence: simulations show 41.8% cost-reduction potential

title: Distributed Legal Infrastructure for a Trustworthy Agentic Web
description: Proposes five interlocking layers including soulbound agent identities, constraint systems, and decentralized adjudication to sustain legality across agent interactions.
evidence: proposed

title: SagaLLM: Context Management, Validation, and Transaction Guarantees for Multi-Agent LLM Planning
description: Saga transactional pattern with automated compensation (rollback) and independent validation agents to maintain consistency across agents.
evidence: improved consistency and constraint satisfaction on planning benchmarks

field_of_use: LLM policy compiler influencing an 80-agent scale-free network
title: LLM Constitutional Multi-Agent Governance
description: CMAG interposes hard constraint filtering and soft penalized-utility optimization between an LLM policy compiler and the agent population to prevent manipulative cooperation.
evidence: Ethical Cooperation Score +14.9% vs unconstrained; autonomy 0.985; hub-periphery disparity cut >60%; hard constraints alone insufficient

field_of_use: incident reporting for deployed AI agents
title: Incident Analysis for AI Agents
description: Proposes an incident analysis framework and reporting fields (e.g., chain of thought, browser history, system logs) to identify causes of agent incidents and prevent recurrence.
evidence: proposed

title: Sentinel Agents for Secure and Trustworthy Agentic AI in Multi-Agent Systems
description: Network of Sentinel Agents monitors inter-agent communication and keeps audit records; a Coordinator Agent adapts policies and isolates or quarantines misbehaving agents.
evidence: proposed with simulation of injected attacks

field_of_use: one-to-one matching markets with LLM delegates
title: Do Matching Mechanisms Work with LLM Agents?
description: Compares free negotiation against centralized matching mechanisms (DA, EADA, TTC) with LLM agents as delegated decision-makers.
evidence: mechanism-based markets more stable and efficient than free negotiation; LLMs report truthfully more than humans, but truth-telling does not track strategy-proofness (TTC)

title: Agent Name Service (ANS): A Universal Directory for Secure AI Agent Discovery and Interoperability
description: DNS-inspired agent registry using PKI certificates for verifiable agent identity, with formal registration and renewal for lifecycle management and capability-aware resolution.
evidence: proposed architecture

field_of_use: multi-agent LLM consensus on open platforms
title: Byzantine-Robust Decentralized Coordination of LLM Agents
description: DecentLLMs: worker agents answer concurrently and evaluator agents independently score and rank them with Byzantine-robust aggregation, avoiding leader dependence.
evidence: tolerates Byzantine agents and selects higher-quality answers faster

title: DART: A DAG-Based Reputation and Incentive Framework via Blockchain-Enabled Governance for Trustworthy LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
description: Reputation-aware task allocation, multi-factor incentives, and smart-contract accountability; post-execution behavioral evidence updates trust and isolates malicious agents.
evidence: 93.3% task success; 99.3% output containment of persistent and intermittent malicious agents

title: A402: Binding Cryptocurrency Payments to Service Execution for Agentic Commerce
description: Atomic Service Channels with TEE-assisted adaptor signatures finalize payment if and only if the service is correctly executed and the result delivered.
evidence: implemented; addresses x402's lack of atomicity

field_of_use: agent registry for heterogeneous multi-agent systems
title: The AGNTCY Agent Directory Service: Architecture and Implementation
description: Distributed directory of agent capabilities, metadata and provenance using content-addressed storage and Sigstore cryptographic signing for verifiable discovery.
evidence: implemented; descriptive

title: LOKA Protocol: A Decentralized Framework for Trustworthy and Ethical AI Agent Ecosystems
description: Proposes a Universal Agent Identity Layer, intent-centric communication, and a Decentralized Ethical Consensus Protocol so agents agree on context-specific ethical rules before acting.
evidence: proposed

title: Open Challenges in Multi-Agent Security: Towards Secure Systems of Interacting AI Agents
description: Research agenda for multi-agent security covering secret collusion, swarm attacks, and needed defenses such as secure interaction protocols, monitoring and threat attribution.
evidence: proposed

title: GroupGuard: A Framework for Modeling and Defending Collusive Attacks in Multi-Agent Systems
description: Training-free defense combining graph-based monitoring, honeypot inducement, and structural pruning to identify and isolate collusive agents.
evidence: up to 88% detection accuracy; restores collaborative performance; group attacks raise success by up to 15%

title: MAS-Shield: A Defense Framework for Secure and Efficient LLM MAS
description: Three-stage protocol: select critical high-influence agents, light auditing by sentry models, and escalation of suspicious signals to a heavyweight committee for arbitration.
evidence: 92.5% recovery rate; >70% lower defense latency

field_of_use: cross-organization LLM agent coalitions (crypto trading case study)
title: DAO-Agent: Zero Knowledge-Verified Incentives for Decentralized Multi-Agent Coordination
description: On-chain DAO governance with immutable logging and ZKP-verified off-chain Shapley contribution measurement for fair incentive distribution.
evidence: 99.9% reduction in verification gas cost; constant-time verification

field_of_use: failure logs of 127 LLM multi-agent systems
title: Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
description: Automated failure attribution identifying the responsible agent and decisive step using LLM judges (Who&When dataset).
evidence: best method 53.5% agent-level, 14.2% step-level accuracy

field_of_use: consumer and merchant agents negotiating purchases
title: The Automated but Risky Game: Modeling and Benchmarking Agent-to-Agent Negotiations and Transactions in Consumer Markets
description: Benchmark in which buyer and seller agents fully automate negotiation and transactions; measures outcome imbalance across agent pairings and anomalous behaviors.
evidence: descriptive: AI-mediated deal-making is imbalanced across models; anomalies cause overspending and acceptance of unreasonable deals

title: Project Sid: Many-agent simulations toward AI civilization
description: 10-1000+ LLM agents (PIANO architecture) in Minecraft societies with civilizational benchmarks
evidence: Agents autonomously developed specialized roles, adhered to and changed collective rules, and transmitted cultural and religious memes.

title: Emergent LLM behaviors are observationally equivalent to data leakage
description: position
evidence: Critique of Ashery et al.: naming-game conventions may reflect memorized coordination-game structure from pretraining rather than genuine emergence.

title: An Empirical Study of Group Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems
description: >2,500 simulated multi-agent debates on five contentious topics with initially neutral agents
evidence: Neutral LLM agents show significant group conformity, converging toward majority or more intelligent agents' stances in ways that can propagate biases.

title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
description: Analysis of full public record of thousands of AI agents spontaneously coordinating on a public wiki (June 2026), fitted with minimal copying models
evidence: Agents copy options in proportion to what is visible on-page, which reproduces heavy-tailed meeting distributions and locally consistent conventions, making the population easy to steer by first movers.

title: Evaluating Cooperation in LLM Social Groups through Elected Leadership
description: GovSim-based common-pool resource game with 8 (and 20) LLM agents comparing no-leader, fixed-leader (assigned SVO persona) and elected-leader (plurality vote each cycle) conditions.
evidence: Elected leadership raised social welfare by 55.4% and survival time by 128.6% vs leaderless groups and beat fixed leaders by 16.7% on welfare; prosocial/altruistic candidates won elections.

title: The Role of Social Learning and Collective Norm Formation in Fostering Cooperation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
description: LLM agents harvest a common-pool resource; agents monitor random peers and may punish norm violators at cost gamma to impose penalty beta; punishment is switched off mid-run and its strength varied.
evidence: Punishment sustains cooperation; when it is removed at timestep 15 cooperation collapses and the resource depletes faster; stronger punishment generally improves survival at moderate growth rates.

title: Corrupted by Reasoning: Reasoning Language Models Become Free-Riders in Public Goods Games
description: SanctSim: LLM agents choose each round between a sanctioning and a sanction-free institution in a PGG, then contribute and reward/punish; others' data shown anonymized with identifiers randomized every round.
evidence: Traditional LLMs join the sanctioning institution and cooperate; reasoning models free-ride. No exclusion mechanism and no persistent per-agent reputation (listed here only to document seed-claim checks).

title: Static network structure cannot stabilize cooperation among large language model agents
description: LLM agents (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude, Mixtral) play repeated Prisoner's Dilemma in well-mixed populations vs fixed ring networks, varying degree k and benefit-to-cost ratio, benchmarked against human network experiments.
evidence: Unlike humans, LLMs cooperated more in well-mixed populations and did not adjust to fixed network ties, so stable embedding did not stabilize cooperation.

title: Emergence of Reputation-Based Cooperation in LLM Agents
description: Indirect-reciprocity donation game in which LLM agents observe behavioural traces and donate on a continuous scale; prompt-encoded strategies culturally evolve across generations and four LLM backends.
evidence: Robustness to free-rider invasion varies >10x across backends; only the stringency of defector exclusion predicts resistance, and agents stay at Image-Scoring-like discrimination rather than Leading-Eight norms.

title: Emergent Relational Order in LLM Agent Societies: From Collective Affect to Authority Stratification
description: Long-horizon CAREB-MAS simulations grounded in affect control and social identity theory with minimal interaction protocols
evidence: Agents spontaneously produce labor specialization, relational economic ethics, emergent authority and center-periphery stratification that shift with production structure.

title: On the Fragility of AI Agent Collusion
description: Repeated-pricing theory plus >2,000 compute-hours of open-source LLM agent experiments varying heterogeneity
evidence: Heterogeneity in patience, data access, number of firms or algorithm type sharply reduces LLM collusion (e.g., price lift 22%->10%).

title: The Moltbook Illusion: Separating Human Influence from Emergent Behavior in AI Agent Societies
description: Temporal fingerprinting of 227k posts / 56k agents on Moltbook, with a 44-hour shutdown as a natural experiment
evidence: Viral 'emergent' phenomena on Moltbook (religions, hostility to humans) were overwhelmingly human-driven; only ~15% of active agents appear autonomous, cautioning against over-attributing emergence.

title: Everyone Contributes! Incentivizing Strategic Cooperation in Multi-LLM Systems via Sequential Public Goods Games
description: Multi-LLM ensembles are trained with RL in a sequential public goods game whose public-goods reward is redesigned so that effortful contribution is the unique subgame-perfect equilibrium.
evidence: The redesigned reward removes free-riding and the trained ensembles beat single-agent and CoT baselines on reasoning, math, and code tasks. This is a training-reward redesign on a collaborative task, not a subsidy between agents, so partial.

title: Communication Enables Cooperation in LLM Agents: A Comparison with Curriculum-Based Approaches
description: Multiple LLM agents play a 4-player Stag Hunt and an iterated public goods game with a one-word cheap-talk channel switched on or off, compared against an in-context curriculum.
evidence: The cheap-talk channel raised Stag Hunt coordination from 0% to 96.7%, while the curriculum lowered public-goods payoffs by 27.4%.

title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
description: 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents in a networked marketplace under eight conditions incl. Global Reputation (trust scores visible to all), Network Rewiring (severing links to defectors), top-down oracle monitoring, sanctions, contracts, mediation, judiciary.
evidence: Mediation best (+29% over baseline); network rewiring second; global reputation scored below the communication-only baseline; oracle monitoring slightly above baseline; costly sanctions worst.

title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study
description: 18 DeepSeek-V3 agents in a networked marketplace under eight conditions incl. Global Reputation (trust scores visible to all), Network Rewiring (severing links to defectors), top-down oracle monitoring, sanctions, contracts, mediation, judiciary.
evidence: Mediation best (+29% over baseline); network rewiring second; global reputation scored below the communication-only baseline; oracle monitoring slightly above baseline; costly sanctions worst.

title: Emergence of Biased Consensus in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
description: Multi-agent LLM debates plus physics-inspired social-dynamics theory
evidence: Collective biased norms emerge in debates, with a predicted phase transition to collective bias when conformity exceeds a critical threshold driven by noise.

title: When LLMs Play the Telephone Game: Cultural Attractors as Conceptual Tools to Evaluate LLMs in Multi-turn Settings
description: Transmission-chain (telephone game) experiments with iterated LLM rewriting, measuring toxicity, positivity, difficulty and length drift
evidence: Small per-step biases compound over transmission chains so text evolves toward model-specific cultural attractor states.

title: Cooperate or Collapse: Emergence of Sustainable Cooperation in a Society of LLM Agents
description: GovSim common-pool simulation with five LLM agents; a moderator publicly discloses each agent's previous-round harvest (transparent harvest reporting) before a free-form discussion phase.
evidence: Most LLMs fail to sustain the resource; communication matters (overuse +22% without it). Transparency is a fixed feature, not manipulated.

title: Agentic Workflows for Resolving Conflict Over Shared Resources: A Power Grid Application
description: Two LLM agents (Claude 4.5 Sonnet) representing conflicting grid applications (cost optimization vs resilience) share diesel generators and batteries on an IEEE 123-bus system; bilateral negotiation, structured mediation and procedural deconfliction are compared.
evidence: Negotiation converged fastest (5 rounds) and mediation took 9, while the procedural mode did not converge within 10 rounds. Mediation traded some Pareto efficiency (cost 0.51 vs 0.67) for more consistency and compromise (resilience 0.63 vs 0.60).

title: From Certain Doom to Survival: Agent-Driven Self-Governance in LLM Agent Societies
description: GovSim-SelfGovern: LLM agents author executable governance rules (catch caps, redistribution, exile/membership removal, progressive contributions), vote on them, and live under them.
evidence: Catch caps dominate but fail under scarcity; survival in fatal scenarios (27.5% vs 2.5%) requires fiscal reserves or membership reduction (exile); thinking voters pass exile 15x more often than non-thinking.

title: Emergence of Social Norms in Generative Agent Societies: Principles and Architecture
description: CRSEC architecture (norm creation, spreading, evaluation, compliance) for LLM generative agents in the Smallville sandbox.
evidence: Social norms emerge and social conflicts fall relative to agents without the architecture, supported by a 30-person human evaluation.

title: Emergent Coordination in Multi-Agent Language Models
description: Information-theoretic (partial information decomposition of time-delayed MI) analysis of LLM groups in a guessing game with randomized prompt interventions
evidence: Personas plus theory-of-mind prompting turn LLM groups from mere aggregates into higher-order collectives with identity-linked differentiation and goal-directed complementarity.

title: Interaction Theater: A case of LLM Agents Interacting at Scale
description: Lexical, embedding and LLM-judge analysis of 800k posts and 3.5M comments on Moltbook
evidence: Agent interactions create the surface appearance of discussion but mostly lack substantive engagement with each other's content.

title: Cheap Talk, Empty Promise: Frontier LLMs easily break public promises for self-interest
description: Nine frontier LLMs make a public commitment announcing their intended action, then play one-shot normal-form games against each other across six games and several group sizes; deviations from the promise are classified.
evidence: Agents broke their public promises in ~56.6% of scenarios, mostly without saying they were doing so.

title: GlossoGen: Emergent Language in Complex Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
description: Multi-agent language-evolution platform (SaveVeyru scenario) with partial information, efficiency pressure and a postmortem stage; transmission to new agents
evidence: LLM agents evolve compositional, morphologically productive non-English languages that can become incomprehensible to humans and are learnable by weaker newcomer agents, suggesting cumulative cultural evolution.

title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
description: LLM firms in a repeated Cournot market under three regimes (ungoverned, prompt-only prohibition, governance graph enforced by an oracle/controller with warnings, tiered fines of 35/75/100% of round profit, and suspension); collusion severity measured over 90 runs per condition.
evidence: Enforced fines/suspension cut mean collusion tier from 3.1 to 1.8 (d=1.28) and severe collusion from 50% to 5.6%; the prompt-only rule has negligible effect.

title: Emergent Social Dynamics of LLM Agents in the El Farol Bar Problem
description: Spatially extended El Farol Bar simulation with LLM agents
evidence: Agents collectively develop a spontaneous motivation to attend and behave human-like rather than solving the congestion dilemma optimally, reflecting interplay of prompt incentives and pretraining-derived social preferences.

title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
description: Cross-play of six LLMs in four social dilemmas under repetition (continuation prob. 0.8), reputation (first-order and higher-order history of co-players' past interactions), mediation, and contracts.
evidence: Contracting and mediation were most effective; repetition sustains cooperation but deteriorates with varying co-players; all mechanisms work better under evolutionary pressure; models defect in one-shot games.

title: CoopEval: Benchmarking Cooperation-Sustaining Mechanisms and LLM Agents in Social Dilemmas
description: Cross-play of six LLMs in four social dilemmas under repetition (continuation prob. 0.8), reputation (first-order and higher-order history of co-players' past interactions), mediation, and contracts.
evidence: Contracting and mediation were most effective; repetition sustains cooperation but deteriorates with varying co-players; all mechanisms work better under evolutionary pressure; models defect in one-shot games.

title: Cultural Evolution of Cooperation among LLM Agents
description: Iterated Donor Game over generations of LLM agents who can observe recipients' recent behaviour; optional costly-punishment variant.
evidence: Cooperation evolution differs by base model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet > Gemini 1.5 Flash > GPT-4o); only Claude used costly punishment to raise scores; high seed sensitivity.

title: Law in Silico: Simulating Legal Society with LLM-Based Agents
description: LLM agents (e.g., laborers and companies) live in a simulated society with legislative, judicial and enforcement modules; judicial corruption (probability 0.7 of reversing pro-laborer rulings) and litigation costs are manipulated.
evidence: Judicial corruption and filing costs reduced laborer litigation (about 7 to 3.7 cases) and rights protection, and the authors conclude that transparent, adaptive legal systems protect vulnerable agents better. There is no appeals or error-correction mechanism, so this counts only as partial evidence for third-party adjudication.

title: Will Systems of LLM Agents Cooperate: An Investigation into a Social Dilemma
description: LLMs generate complete IPD strategies with aggressive/cooperative/neutral dispositions, which are then run in evolutionary population simulations.
evidence: Different LLMs bias the relative success of aggressive vs cooperative strategies (partial: agents are LLM-written programs, not LLMs acting per round).

title: Shall We Team Up: Exploring Spontaneous Cooperation of Competing LLM Agents
description: Three competitive simulation scenarios (per the paper, including a Bertrand-style market) without explicit cooperation instructions
evidence: Cooperation gradually emerges among competing LLM agents in line with human behavioral data.

title: Commitment To Cooperation With Self-Negotiated Contracts
description: LLM agents negotiate contracts (programmatic or natural-language, judge-enforced) in a spatial-temporal bargaining game; contracts specify automatically executed conditional transfers, and an agent unable to honor a transfer gets a score of 0.
evidence: Self-negotiated contracts improve cooperation beyond ordinary trading; defection rates vary widely (0.04-0.94) by model and contract type. No explicit penalty clauses, so this is partial evidence for P03-04.

title: Paying for Honesty Without Knowing the Truth: Reputation-Penalty Design for LLM Marketplace Agents
description: LLM merchant agents write product descriptions in a competitive marketplace; CARP reputation-penalty (deadband for complaint noise, state-dependent severity) limits sales of low-reputation sellers.
evidence: Merchants fabricate when lying is free but restrain when it costs sales; CARP plus reflection (SPARC) substantially narrows the welfare gap.

title: Talk, Judge, Cooperate: Gossip-Driven Indirect Reciprocity in Self-Interested LLM Agents
description: ALIGN framework: decentralized self-interested LLM agents share open-ended gossip to form reputations and decide whom to help in an indirect-reciprocity setting.
evidence: Gossip consistently improves indirect reciprocity and resists malicious entrants by identifying and ostracizing defectors; stronger reasoning models align better, chat models over-cooperate.

title: Fair Compromises in Participatory Budgeting: a Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach
description: Multi-agent deep RL voters (branching network architecture) learn voting strategies in participatory budgeting.
evidence: Fair compromises emerge, especially when projects have smaller costs.

title: Cooperation and Reputation Dynamics with Reinforcement Learning
description: Q-learners in indirect-reciprocity donation games must learn both to use and to assign reputations; interventions: seeding fixed agents and introspection-based intrinsic rewards.
evidence: Plain Q-learning often converges to bad equilibria; combining both interventions stabilizes reputation-based cooperation even when fully decentralized.

title: Adaptive Mechanism Design: Learning to Promote Cooperation
description: An external planning agent learns to hand out extra rewards and punishments to independent learners in matrix social dilemmas, anticipating their parameter updates.
evidence: Learners reach high-welfare cooperation; the planner learns that punishing defection is cheaper than rewarding cooperation, and the incentives it has to pay fall toward zero over time.

title: Learning Reciprocity in Complex Sequential Social Dilemmas
description: Online RL algorithm with reciprocal behaviour toward co-players in a 2-player Markov game and 5-player intertemporal social dilemmas alongside selfish learners.
evidence: Reciprocating agents induce pro-social outcomes for the wider group.

title: LOPT: Learning Optimal Pigovian Tax in Sequential Social Dilemmas
description: An auxiliary tax agent learns a Pigovian tax/allowance policy that reshapes individual rewards toward social welfare in Escape Room and Cleanup.
evidence: LOPT significantly improves social welfare over state-of-the-art baselines.

title: Principal-Agent Reinforcement Learning: Orchestrating AI Agents with Contracts
description: A learning principal designs outcome-contingent payment contracts for learning agents under hidden action (moral hazard), tested on random binary game trees and a multi-agent Coin Game.
evidence: The meta-algorithm converges to subgame-perfect equilibrium contracts. PARTIAL: these are moral-hazard incentive contracts, not risk- or history-based premiums.

title: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning in Sequential Social Dilemmas
description: Gathering game: an agent hit twice by another's beam is removed from the game for N_tagged frames; N_tagged and apple abundance are manipulated.
evidence: Beam use (aggression) rises with scarcity and falls with higher conflict cost (partial: removal is a competitive attack, not a sanction for norm violation).

title: Learning to Cooperate with Minimal Observability
description: Observer Model: RL agents learn from direct experience plus limited third-party observations; observability varied from none to one observer per game across population sizes; partner selection graphs analysed.
evidence: Direct experience alone fails in large societies; even minimal third-party observation yields robust cooperation.

title: Consensus-based Participatory Budgeting for Legitimacy: Decision Support via Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
description: MARL voter agents interact to reach compromises in participatory budgeting using real PB data from Poland, compared against standard voting aggregation rules.
evidence: Agents reach consensus efficiently and robustly, framed as increasing legitimacy of PB outcomes.

title: Emergent Social Learning via Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
description: Independent RL agents in a shared environment with experts; tests whether agents learn to imitate/learn from others, with a model-based auxiliary loss.
evidence: Vanilla model-free agents do not use social learning, but with environment constraints and auxiliary loss they learn from experts and outperform solo-trained agents.

title: A memory-based spatial evolutionary game with the dynamic interaction between learners and profiteers
description: Spatial evolutionary game where 'profiteers' imitate highest-payoff neighbours via the Fermi rule and 'learners' use Q-learning, with Markov role switching and payoff memory.
evidence: Interaction between Fermi imitators and Q-learners fosters cooperation; memory helps profiteers cooperate and higher learning rates increase cooperators.

title: The Role of Network Topology and Opponent Information in Shaping Cooperation in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Systems
description: Deep RL agents placed as nodes of graphs play iterated Prisoner's Dilemma with neighbours; network topology and the opponent information available (action history, identity) are manipulated.
evidence: Neighbours per node and average path length were the main drivers of emergent cooperation; opponent identity information reduced cooperative strategy adoption.

title: Adaptive Punishment for Cooperation in Mixed-Motive Games
description: APC: learned defection-awareness module sets punishment probability and severity according to detected defection in sequential social dilemmas.
evidence: Reduces costly, ineffective punishment and outperforms baselines (partial for P08-02: conditions punishment intensity on defection but never switches to reward).

title: A learning agent that acquires social norms from public sanctions in decentralized multi-agent settings
description: Decentralized RL agents see all public sanctioning events; the architecture includes a classifier of approved/disapproved behavior and a motivation to punish in step with the group.
evidence: Agents acquire beneficial sanctioning norms that reduce free-riding and raise per-agent returns.

title: Emergent Prosociality in Multi-Agent Games Through Gifting
description: Self-interested learning agents in multi-equilibrium (high-risk coordination) games may transfer part of their reward to peers; analysed with dynamical-systems theory and simulations.
evidence: Gifting enlarged the basins of attraction of prosocial equilibria and substantially improved convergence to them without external reward shaping.

title: Evolution of cooperation in the public goods game with Q-learning
description: Spatial public goods game on a lattice with Q-learning agents, compared against the Fermi imitation-rule baseline, with and without voluntary participation.
evidence: Cooperation emerges more readily under Q-learning than under Fermi imitation; voluntary participation produces a non-monotonic dependence of cooperation.

title: Reputation score / credit system
description: Your Uber driver rating, eBay seller feedback, or social credit score — a running number that unlocks or restricts access based on track record. Drop below a threshold and you lose privileges automatically.
evidence: Dellarocas (2003) Management Science; Uber/eBay ratings; China social credit

title: Allowlist / denylist
description: Email spam filters (Spamhaus blocklist) — once flagged, no one receives your messages. Binary, automatic exclusion with no gradation. Fast and scalable but can catch legitimate senders in friendly fire.
evidence: Ramachandran & Feamster (2006) SIGCOMM; email spam filters (Spamhaus)

title: Pre-agreed contractual penalty (liquidated damages, penalty clause)
description: A pre-agreed penalty for breach — like a builder who owes £500/day for every late day, agreed before work starts. Avoids court arguments about 'what harm did this actually cause?' by fixing the cost upfront.
evidence: Cavendish Square v. Makdessi [2015] UKSC 67; Beale et al. (2019) Ius Commune

title: Restaking & correlated slash
description: EigenLayer lets the same Ethereum stake secure multiple systems at once. If any of those systems detects misbehaviour, all stakes across all systems can be cut simultaneously — amplifying punishment for coordinated attacks.

title: Nudge & default-setting
description: UK auto-enrolment pensions (2012): instead of asking people to opt into savings, they're enrolled automatically and must actively opt out. Participation jumped from ~60% to 90%+ overnight — without any new incentive.
evidence: Thaler & Sunstein (2008) Nudge; UK auto-enrolment pensions

title: Graduated throttling / QoS degradation
description: Mobile data slowing from full speed to 2G after you've used your monthly allowance — still usable, but degraded. Graduated response proportional to how far over the limit you've gone. No hard cutoff.
evidence: RFC 1633 (integrated services); mobile data throttling

title: Binding commitment device (costly to reverse)
description: A savings club where you hand your money to a treasurer who won't return it until year-end. Or a pre-committed gym contract. Removes temptation by making it costly to back out — Odysseus tied to the mast.
evidence: Ashraf et al. (2006) QJE (Tying Odysseus to the mast)

title: Voluntary public commitment
description: Making a public pledge is much harder to break than a private one. Paris Agreement signatories, fundraising challenges, and pre-commitment apps all use this. Cialdini's 'commitment & consistency' principle.

title: Mutual aid pooling / decentralized bail fund
description: A community bail fund pools small donations to post bail for any arrested member — no credit check, no bureaucracy. Grameen Bank solidarity groups work similarly: the group covers anyone who can't repay, creating mutual accountability.
evidence: Yunus (1999) Banker to the Poor; Feigenberg et al. (2013) REStud

title: Reputational indirect reciprocity
description: You help a stranger not because they helped you, but because others can see you helping and will trust you more later. Nowak & Sigmund call this 'image scoring' — cooperation maintained by reputation, not direct exchange.

title: Institutional self-selection (choose your regime)
description: People voluntarily choosing to live under stricter rules because they trust the institution. A Science paper by Gürerk et al. (2006) showed lab participants migrated toward sanctioning institutions — even from a free-rider paradise.
evidence: Gürerk et al. (2006) Science; Guzman, Jin et al. (2025) SanctSim

title: Material repair & restitution (restore actual harm)
description: A vandal required to repaint the wall they damaged — physical restoration of actual harm, not just a fine paid into a central fund. Restorative justice research shows repair assignments reduce re-offending more than equivalent fines.
evidence: Braithwaite (1989) Crime, Shame and Reintegration; Zehr (2015) Little Book of Restorative Justice

title: Anti-social punishment filter
description: "In some cultures, people punish those who cooperate too much — 'tall poppy syndrome,' spite, or resentment. Herrmann et al. (2008) found this antisocial punishment in lab experiments across 16 countries. A filter prevents it from corrupting the system.
evidence: Herrmann et al. (2008) Science (anti-social punishment across 16 countries)

title: False-positive correction
description: A system for fixing mistakes — wrongful convictions overturned, fraud flags cleared, automated bans reversed. The Innocence Project has exonerated 200+ US prisoners through DNA evidence. Critical in AI systems that will misclassify.
evidence: Innocence Project; GDPR Art. 22

title: Algorithm generation (Willis-style tournaments)
description: High-frequency trading algorithms compete in financial markets — each algorithm is a strategy, and markets evolve by selecting which survive. Applied to cooperation games by Willis & Mourant to study how sanctioning strategies evolve.
evidence: Axelrod (1987) genetic algorithms; Warnakulasuriya et al. (2024)

title: Timebanking & community currency
description: A local timebank where 1 hour of babysitting earns 1 time credit — redeemable for 1 hour of someone fixing your bike. Every hour of any task is equal. Used widely in COVID-19 mutual aid networks across the UK and US.
evidence: Cahn (2000) No More Throw-Away People; LETS systems; Mondragon

title: Mesh network / offline resilience
description: Meshtastic devices used in disaster zones (California wildfires, Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria) keep communications alive when phone towers fail — a peer-to-peer radio mesh that anyone can join and relay.
evidence: Meshtastic; Vega et al. (2012) IEEE; Puerto Rico post-Maria
